# Standard Makefile

The Makefile is a thin, uniform front door: the same `make <name>` does the same kind of thing in every repository, and each target calls whatever the repo already uses. Standardize the names, not the implementation.

## Standard targets

Define only the ones the repository can actually do. Each line is the canonical target, then the aliases that must point at it.

| Target | Does | Aliases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `help` | Default goal; lists the targets | |
| `setup` | Install dependencies and tools, once | `install` |
| `run` | Start the app locally as it normally runs: server, service or CLI | `start`, `serve` |
| `dev` | Start it in development mode (watch, hot reload, debug); only when that differs from `run`, never an alias of it | |
| `test` | Run the test suite | `tests` |
| `lint` | Static checks, no changes | |
| `format` | Apply formatting | `fmt` |
| `check` | Everything CI gates on, usually `lint` and `test`; only when it runs more than one target | |
| `build` | Produce the deployable artefact | |
| `clean` | Remove generated output | |

Any other task keeps a descriptive name of its own (`release`, `film`, `migrate`).

## Steps

1. **Inventory.** Find every way the repository is run today:
   ```bash
   ls Makefile makefile GNUmakefile justfile Taskfile.yml package.json pyproject.toml Cargo.toml go.mod 2>/dev/null
   grep -nE '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+:' Makefile 2>/dev/null
   python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("package.json")).get("scripts", {}))' 2>/dev/null
   ls scripts bin 2>/dev/null
   git grep -hoE '(make [a-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*|npm (run )?[a-z]+|yarn [a-z]+|pnpm [a-z]+|uv run [^`]+|poetry run [^`]+|python3? [A-Za-z0-9_/.-]+\.py|\./scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)' -- '*.md' '*.yml' '*.yaml' | sort | uniq -c
   ```
   Read the existing Makefile in full if there is one.

2. **Map each command to a target.** Write a short list: standard target or descriptive name, and the command it runs. An existing target whose name is an alias in the table (for example `serve`) is renamed to the canonical target, and the old name becomes an alias, so existing habits and docs keep working. The target keeps its body and description. If two existing commands compete for one target (two ways to start the app), pick the one the README and CI use and give the other a descriptive name.

3. **Write or extend the Makefile.** Keep it plain:
   - Targets call the existing scripts and tools; do not reimplement their logic in make. Variables only for values a person overrides (`PORT ?= 8000`).
   - Every real target has a `## description` comment on its rule line; aliases have none, so `help` lists each command once.
   - Put the aliases in one block near the top so they are easy to see.
   - When a target needs a running service (tests against a dev server), start and stop it inside the target.

   Shape to follow:
   ```make
   .DEFAULT_GOAL := help
   .PHONY: help setup run test clean install start serve tests

   install: setup
   start serve: run
   tests: test

   help: ## List the targets
   	@grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk -F':.*## ' '{printf "  make %-10s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

   setup: ## Install dependencies
   	uv sync

   run: ## Start the app at http://localhost:8000/
   	uv run app

   test: ## Run the tests
   	uv run pytest
   ```
   Extending an existing Makefile: rename and alias as mapped in step 2, add the missing standard targets the repo supports, add `help` and `## ` comments, and leave every other target as it is.

4. **Remove wrappers that only duplicate the Makefile.** A `package.json`, `justfile` or shell script whose only job is to call commands that are now targets goes, and its commands move into the Makefile. Keep it when it is real configuration for its own toolchain (a Node project's `package.json` stays, and the targets call `npm`). If you are unsure whether anything else depends on a file, ask before deleting it.

5. **Point the docs at make.** Replace the old commands in the README, the agent instructions (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`) and contributor docs with the targets. Change CI to call targets only where it already runs the same command; do not restructure CI.

6. **Verify.**
   ```bash
   make                    # prints help, one line per real target
   make -n <target>        # for every target: prints the command it would run
   ```
   Then run `make setup` and `make test` (or `make check`) for real. Start `make run` in the background, confirm it responds (`curl` its port, or its first output for a CLI), and stop it. Each must behave exactly as the command it replaced; fix any target that does not before committing. If a run rewrites tracked files (snapshots, screenshots), restore them with `git checkout -- <path>` and tell the user, rather than committing the noise.
